description.sr:
Napiši tip `DeepReadonly<T>` koji svako svojstvo objekta, uključujući ugnježdene objekte, pravi `readonly`.

Funkcije ostaju kakve jesu, a primitivni tipovi se ne menjaju.

Primer:
```ts
type X = { a: number; b: { c: string } };
type R = DeepReadonly<X>; // { readonly a: number; readonly b: { readonly c: string } }
```

Ne izvršava se nikakav kod: rešenje je tačno kad nema grešaka tipova.
description.en:
Write a type `DeepReadonly<T>` that makes every property of an object `readonly`, including nested objects.

Functions stay as they are, and primitive types are not changed.

Example:
```ts
type X = { a: number; b: { c: string } };
type R = DeepReadonly<X>; // { readonly a: number; readonly b: { readonly c: string } }
```

No code is executed: the solution is correct when there are no type errors.

hiddenTests: type Case3 = Expect<Equal<DeepReadonly<{ f: () => void }>['f'], () => void>>;

text.sr:
Prva provera: da li je `T` funkcija?

- `type DeepReadonly<T> = ...` pravi alias sa jednim parametrom tipa. Ceo tip je jedan lanac uslova, kao `if / else if / else`: linije 1 do 5.
- `T extends (...args: never[]) => unknown` pita: „da li je `T` bilo kakva funkcija?“.
- `(...args: never[]) => unknown` je tip „funkcija sa bilo kojim parametrima koja vraća bilo šta“. `never[]` se koristi jer parametri funkcija idu u suprotnom smeru: funkcija koja prima bilo šta može da se dodeli onoj koja prima `never`, pa taj tip prihvata sve funkcije.
text.en:
The first check: is `T` a function?

- `type DeepReadonly<T> = ...` creates an alias with one type parameter. The whole type is one chain of conditions, like `if / else if / else`: lines 1 to 5.
- `T extends (...args: never[]) => unknown` asks: “is `T` any kind of function?”.
- `(...args: never[]) => unknown` is the type “a function with any parameters that returns anything”. `never[]` is used because function parameters go in the opposite direction: a function that accepts anything can be assigned to one that accepts `never`, so this type accepts all functions.

text.sr:
Ako je funkcija, ostaje nepromenjena (`? T`).

- `? T` je grana „da“ iz prethodnog uslova: rezultat je isti tip `T`.
- Funkcije su u JavaScript-u i objekti, pa bi ih sledeća grana (`extends object`) mapirala i dobili bismo `{}`, čime bi se izgubio potpis funkcije.
- Zato se funkcije izdvajaju PRE provere za objekte (skriveni test proverava `() => void`).
text.en:
If it is a function, it stays unchanged (`? T`).

- `? T` is the “yes” branch of the previous condition: the result is the same type `T`.
- Functions in JavaScript are objects too, so the next branch (`extends object`) would map them and we would get `{}`, losing the function's signature.
- That is why functions are separated BEFORE the check for objects (the hidden test checks `() => void`).

text.sr:
Druga provera: da li je `T` objekat?

- `: T extends object` je „u suprotnom, ako...“ deo lanca.
- `object` obuhvata obične objekte i nizove. Primitivi (`number`, `string`, `boolean`) nisu objekti.
text.en:
The second check: is `T` an object?

- `: T extends object` is the “otherwise, if...” part of the chain.
- `object` covers plain objects and arrays. Primitives (`number`, `string`, `boolean`) are not objects.

text.sr:
Objekat: svako svojstvo postaje `readonly`, rekurzivno.

- `[K in keyof T]` je mapirani tip: prolazi kroz svaki ključ `K` iz `keyof T` (unija imena svojstava) i pravi svojstvo istog imena.
- `readonly` ispred zabranjuje promenu tog svojstva posle kreiranja.
- `DeepReadonly<T[K]>` je **rekurzija**: isti tip se primenjuje na tip svakog svojstva. Zato i ugnježdeni objekti (`b.d.e`) postaju `readonly`, a ne samo prvi nivo.
text.en:
An object: every property becomes `readonly`, recursively.

- `[K in keyof T]` is a mapped type: it goes through every key `K` of `keyof T` (a union of the property names) and creates a property with the same name.
- `readonly` in front forbids changing that property after creation.
- `DeepReadonly<T[K]>` is **recursion**: the same type is applied to the type of every property. That is why nested objects (`b.d.e`) become `readonly` too, not just the first level.

text.sr:
Sve ostalo ostaje isto (`: T`).

- To su primitivi: `number`, `string`, `boolean`... Njih nema smisla „zaključavati“, jer se ne menjaju iznutra.
- Ovo je i izlaz iz rekurzije: tipovi bez svojstava se vraćaju takvi kakvi jesu.
- `;` završava deklaraciju aliasa.

Kako se računa `DeepReadonly<{ a: number; b: { c: string } }>`:

```
T nije funkcija → T je objekat → mapira se svako svojstvo:
  a: DeepReadonly<number>        → number nije funkcija ni objekat → number
  b: DeepReadonly<{ c: string }> → objekat → { readonly c: DeepReadonly<string> = string }

rezultat: { readonly a: number; readonly b: { readonly c: string } }
```
text.en:
Everything else stays the same (`: T`).

- These are primitives: `number`, `string`, `boolean`... There is no point in “locking” them, since they cannot be changed from inside.
- This is also the exit from the recursion: types without properties are returned as they are.
- `;` ends the alias declaration.

How `DeepReadonly<{ a: number; b: { c: string } }>` is computed:

```
T is not a function → T is an object → every property is mapped:
  a: DeepReadonly<number>        → number is neither a function nor an object → number
  b: DeepReadonly<{ c: string }> → object → { readonly c: DeepReadonly<string> = string }

result: { readonly a: number; readonly b: { readonly c: string } }
```

note.sr: Funkcije se moraju izuzeti pre provere `extends object`, jer su i one objekti, pa bi mapiranje preko njih dalo `{}`.
note.en: Functions must be excluded before the `extends object` check, because they are objects too and mapping over them would give `{}`.
